To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) collaborative ethnography is a powerful tool for understanding and addressing complex social issues, (b) video is an excellent medium for public dissemination of collaborative ethnographic research, (c) video is an effective medium for engaging both academic and public stakeholders in a dialogic conversation about the issues being researched, and (d) video can be used to assess the quality and impact of collaborative ethnographic work.

1) the public and academic audiences are interested in and can benefit from a public ethnographic approach to research, 2) public ethnographic research can be conducted in a rigorous and transparent manner, and 3) there is a need for a new set of criteria for evaluating the quality of public research.

the use of video in collaborative ethnography is a useful and powerful way to disseminate research findings to public audiences and can be a useful tool for researchers to use in peer review processes and for the purposes of promotion, tenure, and awarding degrees.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the ways in which the public and the academy are connected, and how they can be more effectively connected to address the challenges of the twenty-first century.
understanding how to do and disseminate collaborative public ethnography, and how to do so in ways that are of quality, and that are both academically and publicly relevant.
how to assess quality and rigor in a public ethnography that is not only accessible and relevant to public audiences, but also to academic audiences.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the quality of collaborative ethnography, as a form of public ethnography, is not necessarily determined by the traditional academic standards, such as peer review, but by the degree to which the research is accessible to and useful to a public audience.
the quality of public science can be assessed and evaluated, and that the academy should support such efforts.

the quality of collaborative public ethnography is a question of process, which includes a commitment to the principles of collaborative ethnography as well as to the principles of public ethnography.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are attempting to use the tools of science to address the needs of the public and the tools of art to address the needs for science.
the use of a video documentary to disseminate our research was effective at engaging public audiences, but it was also effective at engaging academic audiences.

we have been successful in creating a collaborative ethnographic research team and in developing and implementing a video ethnography project that has been well received by our public audiences, and that has the potential to make a positive contribution to our community.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the quality of publically relevant and collaborative ethnographic work can be assessed using the same standards as traditional ethnographic work and that the process of peer review should be expanded to include a broader range of audiences.
the academy can support public ethnography by creating spaces for dialogic and collaborative dissemination, which can be used to address public issues, such as health and education.
it is possible for social science researchers to do and disseminate quality public ethnography using nontraditional modes of dissemination.
